record_identity.title: OpenAI routing error caused elevated errors across ChatGPT and Codex on 3 September 2026

incident_identity.historical_event_name: 3 September 2026 ChatGPT and Codex elevated-errors outage
incident_identity.date_basis: OpenAI Status records the incident on 3 September 2026, with investigation beginning at 14:43 UTC, mitigation by 15:17 UTC and resolution at 16:55 UTC; an OpenAI spokesperson separately attributed user unavailability beginning around 07:43 PT to a routing error.

summary: OpenAI reported elevated errors across ChatGPT and Codex on 3 September 2026. The provider status page listed 15 affected ChatGPT components and four Codex components, and the incident was resolved after roughly two hours. OpenAI separately told The Register that a routing error made ChatGPT and Codex unavailable for some users across platforms. The outage overlapped with availability incidents at Anthropic and xAI, but no common cause is established and this Incident records only the OpenAI occurrence.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: OpenAI's public status record establishes a resolved degraded-performance incident affecting ChatGPT and Codex on 3 September 2026, including 15 ChatGPT components and four Codex components. OpenAI stated to The Register that a routing error beginning around 07:43 PT made ChatGPT and Codex unavailable for some users across platforms and that a solution was implemented around 08:17 PT. Independent reporting documented overlapping Claude and Grok outages during the same period but also reported that Cloudflare and the major public-cloud status pages did not show a relevant shared disruption. No evidence presently establishes that the provider outages shared one technical cause.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: This is a bounded service-availability occurrence with a provider-attributed routing mechanism. It is relevant to operational resilience, dependency management and recovery controls, but the current public evidence does not establish a failure mechanism that can be mapped defensibly to a current VIGIL Failure Class without extending beyond the occurrence-level facts. It therefore remains unclassified.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence illustrates operational dependence on frontier AI services and the need for resilience, fallback and availability controls where ChatGPT or Codex are embedded in organisational workflows. The contemporaneous but causally unresolved outages at other providers are ecosystem context rather than evidence of a shared dependency failure.
assessment_boundaries: The number of affected users, organisations and transactions is not publicly quantified by OpenAI.
The provider's public status page does not publish a full root-cause analysis beyond the routing-error statement reported by The Register.
The overlapping Anthropic and xAI outages are not treated as one incident and no shared cloud, network or control-plane cause is inferred.
No data-loss, confidentiality, integrity, safety or persistent downstream harm is established by the reviewed sources.

severity_assessment.materialised_consequence: ChatGPT and Codex experienced elevated errors and temporary unavailability for some users across platforms until OpenAI applied mitigation and restored service.
severity_assessment.affected_scope: OpenAI listed 15 ChatGPT components and four Codex components as affected. The number and geography of affected users and organisations were not quantified.
severity_assessment.seriousness_and_persistence: The incident materially impaired access to widely used hosted AI services for roughly two hours, but OpenAI reported recovery the same day and no persistent service, data, safety or integrity consequence is established.
severity_assessment.quantitative_information: OpenAI listed 15 affected ChatGPT components and four Codex components. The public status record spans approximately 14:43–16:55 UTC on 3 September 2026. Affected-user counts and transaction volumes were not published.
severity_assessment.evidentiary_limits: Public evidence establishes degraded availability and a provider-attributed routing error but not a complete causal chain, affected-user count, economic loss, downstream organisational harm or common cause with other providers' outages.
severity_assessment.band_rationale: S3 is supported because the occurrence caused material but time-bounded loss of availability across multiple core service components and affected some users across platforms. S2 is not supported because no serious or persistent downstream harm, safety consequence, data compromise or extended systemic disruption is established. S4 would understate the occurrence because provider-confirmed service unavailability affected numerous core ChatGPT and Codex components rather than a trivial or purely cosmetic defect.
